_doc.purpose: Human rulings on award-record names the matching rules in src/build_venues.py will not decide for themselves. Same role config/recognition_suppress.json plays for the dashboard: the rules stay conservative, and a person's answer goes here rather than into a lowered threshold.
_doc.why_not_just_loosen_the_rules: Every one of these is one edit away from a rule that would also mis-handle a real name. 'Zaab Zaab, Zaab Zaab Talay' is two restaurants in one string; 'Fifty Seven Fifty Seven, The Four Seasons Hotel' and "Lorenzo's Restaurant, Bar & Cabaret" are single restaurants with the identical shape. A rule that splits the first splits the other two, and those failures are invisible. Three hand rulings cost nothing and break nothing.
_doc.how_to_add: Run src/build_venues.py and read data/processed/venue_merge_review.json, or look for a venue whose name is plainly not a restaurant. Add it here with a reason, re-run, and confirm the row is gone.

not_venues._doc: Award-record names that are people, companies or publications rather than restaurants. The award record is DROPPED with its reason recorded -- no venue is created, and nothing is silently attached to a real restaurant instead.
A bartender's company. The award is to Dale DeGroff, who has no restaurant in these files.
not_venues.Founders, \"Food & Wine\" and \"Food Art: Two magazines. The award is to their founders, not to a room.
not_venues.B.R. Guests Restaurants: A restaurant group's corporate name; the rooms it names are handled by the group-award split.
not_venues.Red Cat Restaurants: A restaurant group's corporate name, same as above.
not_venues.Elizabeth Street Hospitality: A restaurant group's corporate name, same as above.
not_venues.Gracious Hospitality: A restaurant group's corporate name, same as above.
not_venues.Gracious Hospitality Management: A restaurant group's corporate name, same as above.
not_venues.Overthrow Hospitality: A restaurant group's corporate name, same as above.
not_venues.Matsuhisa: The Los Angeles restaurant named alongside Nobu in "Nobu, NY/Matsuhisa, LA". A real restaurant and a real award, but not in New York, and this roster is a New York roster. Reachable only since the slash became a separator: it used to be hidden inside the part "NY/Matsuhisa", which was refused for containing a slash -- the right answer for the wrong reason.
not_venues.Rosenthal Wine Merchant/Mad Rose Group: An importer and a wine group, for Outstanding Wine & Spirits Professional. Neither half is a room you can book, so unlike the other slash-separated records there is nothing here to split out.

split_into._doc: Strings that ARE a list of restaurants, where the automatic split cannot prove it because fewer than two parts are already on the roster. The named parts each get the award, and each becomes a venue if it is not one already -- which is safe here precisely because a human has confirmed the split.
